arxiv-2104-12133.title: What About the Precedent: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Common Law
arxiv-2104-12133.creator: Josef Valvoda Tiago Pimentel Niklas Stoehr Ryan Cotterell Simone Teufel
arxiv-2104-12133.description: Abstract In common law, the outcome of a new case is determined mostly by precedent cases, rather than by existing statutes. However, how exactly does the precedent influence the outcome of a new case? Answering this question is crucial for guaranteeing fair and consistent judicial decision-making.

arxiv-2107-08050.creator: L. G. Bouma, J. L. Curtis, J. D. Hartman, J. N. Winn, G. Á. Bakos
arxiv-2107-08050.description: Abstract Recent analyses of the Gaia data have identified diffuse stellar populations surrounding nearby open clusters. It is important to verify that these “halos”, “tails”, and “strings” are of similar ages and compositions as stars in the denser part of the cluster.

arxiv-2202-01990.title: Ion partitioning effect on the electrostatic interaction between two charged soft surfaces Volume: 00
arxiv-2202-01990.creator: Jun-Sik Sin
arxiv-2202-01990.description: Abstract We theoretically investigate electrostatic properties between two charged surfaces with a grafted polyelectrolyte layer in an aqueous electrolyte solution by using the Poisson-Boltzmann approach accounting for ion partitioning. In order to consider the ion partitioning effect, we focus on changes of electrostatic properties due to the difference in dielectric permittivity of the polyelectrolyte layer and the aqueous electrolyte solution.

arxiv-2208-14796.title: 3DLG-Detector: 3D Object Detection via Simultaneous Local-Global Feature Learning
arxiv-2208-14796.creator: Baian Chen, Liangliang Nan, Haoran Xie, Dening Lu, Fu Lee Wang, Mingqiang Wei
arxiv-2208-14796.description: Abstract Capturing both local and global features of irregular point clouds is essential to 3D object detection (3OD). However, mainstream 3D detectors, e.g., VoteNet and its variants, either abandon considerable local features during pooling operations or ignore many global features in the whole scene context.

arxiv-2301-02324.title: Reasoning about Causality in Games Published in Artificial Intelligence . DOI: 10.1016/j.artint.2023.103919 . Correspondence to lewis.hammond@cs.ox.ac.uk and james.fox@cs.ox.ac.uk .
arxiv-2301-02324.creator: Lewis Hammond, James Fox, Tom Everitt, Ryan Carey, Alessandro Abate, Michael Wooldridge
arxiv-2301-02324.description: Abstract Abstract [] Causal reasoning and game-theoretic reasoning are fundamental topics in artificial intelligence, among many other disciplines: this paper is concerned with their intersection. Despite their importance, a formal framework that supports both these forms of reasoning has, until now, been lacking.

This paper is concerned with a non-autonomous sup-cubic semilinear wave equation in a smooth bounded domain of ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} , using the introduced weak topology entropy, we obtain an upper bound for the ε \varepsilon -entropy of the uniform attractor for the case where the external forces are not translation-compact.

arxiv-2303-05675.title: HumanBench: Towards General Human-centric Perception with Projector Assisted Pretraining
arxiv-2303-05675.creator: Shixiang Tang, Cheng Chen, Qingsong Xie, Meilin Chen, Yizhou Wang, Yuanzheng Ci, Lei Bai, Feng Zhu, Haiyang Yang, Li Yi, Rui Zhao, Wanli Ouyang
arxiv-2303-05675.description: Abstract Human-centric perceptions include a variety of vision tasks, which have widespread industrial applications, including surveillance, autonomous driving, and the metaverse. It is desirable to have a general pretrain model for versatile human-centric downstream tasks. This paper forges ahead along this path from the aspects of both benchmark and pretraining methods.

arxiv-2402-19023.title: Jointly Learning Selection Matrices for Transmitters, Receivers and Fourier Coefficients in Multichannel Imaging
arxiv-2402-19023.description: Abstract Strategic subsampling has become a focal point due to its effectiveness in compressing data, particularly in the Full Matrix Capture (FMC) approach in ultrasonic imaging. This paper introduces the Joint Deep Probabilistic Subsampling (J-DPS) method, which aims to learn optimal selection matrices simultaneously for transmitters, receivers, and Fourier coefficients.

arxiv-2406-13403.title: Joint qubit observables induced by indirect measurements in cavity QED
arxiv-2406-13403.creator: Kalle Raikisto, Kimmo Luoma
arxiv-2406-13403.description: Abstract A fundamental feature of quantum mechanics is that there are observables which can be measured jointly only when some noise is added to them. Their sharp versions are said to be incompatible. In this work we investigate time-continuous joint qubit observables induced by a indirect time-continuous measurements.

arxiv-2410-07744.title: Modularity maximization and community detection in complex networks through recursive and hierarchical annealing in the DWAVE Advantage quantum processing units
arxiv-2410-07744.creator: Joan Falcó-Roget, Kacper Jurek, Barbara Wojtarowicz, Karol Capała, Katarzyna Rycerz
arxiv-2410-07744.description: Abstract Quantum adiabatic optimization has long been expected to outperform classical methods in solving NP-type problems. While this has been proven in certain experiments, its main applications still reside in academic problems where the size of the system to be solved would not represent an obstacle to any modern desktop computer.

arxiv-2410-23636.title: Imaging of the Vega Debris System using JWST/MIRI Facilities: JWST(MIRI)
arxiv-2410-23636.creator: Kate Y. L. Su, András Gáspár, George H. Rieke, Renu Malhotra, Luca Matrá, Schuyler Grace Wolff, Jarron M. Leisenring, Charles Beichman, Marie Ygouf
arxiv-2410-23636.description: Abstract We present images of the Vega planetary debris disk obtained at 15.5, 23, and 25.5 μ \mu m with the Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) on JWST. The debris system is remarkably symmetric and smooth, and centered accurately on the star.

arxiv-2510-10961.title: KOTOX: A Korean Toxic Dataset for Deobfuscation and Detoxification
arxiv-2510-10961.creator: Yejin Lee, Su-Hyeon Kim, Hyundong Jin, Kim Dayoung, Kim Yeon Soo, Yo-Sub Han
arxiv-2510-10961.description: Abstract Toxic content has become an increasingly critical social issue with the rapid expansion of online communication. While numerous studies explored methods for detecting and detoxifying such content, most have focused primarily on English, leaving low-resource language underrepresented. Consequently, Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle to identify and neutralize toxic expressions in these languages.

arxiv-2510-22502.title: Rationality of cycles modulo 2 on products of generically smooth quadrics in characteristic 2
arxiv-2510-22502.creator: Stephen Scully, Guangzhao Zhu
arxiv-2510-22502.description: Abstract . A 2022 result of Karpenko establishes a conjecture of Hoffmann-Totaro on the possible values of the first higher isotropy index of an arbitrary anisotropic quadratic form of given dimension over an arbitrary field. For nondegenerate forms, this essentially goes back to a 2003 article of the same author on quadratic forms over fields of characteristic not 2.

pmc-11351933.title: Characterization of the Secretome from Spheroids of Adipose-Derived Stem Cells (SASCs) and Its Potential for Tissue Regeneration
pmc-11351933.creator: Valentina Urrata, Francesca Toia, Emanuele Cammarata, Mara Franza, Luigi Montesano, Adriana Cordova, Anna Barbara Di Stefano
pmc-11351933.description: Introduction: Spheroids are spherical aggregates of cells that mimic the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of tissues more closely than traditional two dimensional (2D) cultures. Spheroids of adipose stem cells (SASCs) show special features such as high multilineage differentiation potential and immunomodulatory activity. These properties have been attributed to their secreted factors, such as cytokines and growth factors.

pmc-11636205.title: Airborne Tire Wear Particles: A Critical Reanalysis of the Literature Reveals Emission Factors Lower than Expected
pmc-11636205.creator: Siriel Saladin, Adam Boies, Chiara Giorio
pmc-11636205.description: Tires are a ubiquitous part of on-road transport systems serving as the critical connecting component at the interface of the motive power and road surface. While tires are essential to automobile function, the wear of tires as a source of particulate air pollution is still poorly understood.

pmc-11672278.title: E2F2 Reprograms Macrophage Function By Modulating Material and Energy Metabolism in the Progression of Metabolic Dysfunction‐Associated Steatohepatitis
pmc-11672278.creator: Zheng Liu, Hao Wang, Yuan Liang, Mu Liu, Qiyuan Huang, Mingming Wang, Jinren Zhou, Qingfa Bu, Haoming Zhou, Ling Lu
pmc-11672278.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Macrophages are essential for the development of steatosis, hepatic inflammation, and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatohepatitis(MASH). However, the roles of macrophage E2F2 in the progression of MASH have not been elucidated. This study reveals that the expression of macrophage E2F2 is dramatically downregulated in MASH livers from mice and humans, and that this expression is adversely correlated with the severity of the disease. Myeloid‐specific E2F2 depletion aggravates intrahepatic inflammation, hepatic stellate cell activation, and hepatocyte lipid accumulation during MASH progression.

pmc-12712131.title: Systemic amyloid A amyloidosis in a captive Cape hyrax (Procavia capensis)
pmc-12712131.creator: Aya TERAO, Susumu IWAIDE, Natsumi KOBAYASHI, Tomoaki MURAKAMI, Yoshiyuki ITOH, Masakazu NAKADA, Tomoyuki SHIBAHARA
pmc-12712131.description: Amyloidosis is a disease caused by amyloid deposition and has been reported in various animal species; however, reports on Afrotherian species, including Cape hyraxes, are extremely limited. In this report, we describe the case of a 4-year-old captive Cape hyrax affected by amyloidosis.

pmc-13511458.description: IntroductionHuman papillomavirus (HPV) associated cancers constitute a major global health concern, particularly among people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Accumulating evidence suggests that HPV-HIV co-infection substantially increases the risk of genital, cervical, and oral cancers; however, the molecular and immunological mechanisms underlying this association remain incompletely elucidated.
